texts.preamble: Shri U. Udaiyar vs The Andaman And Nicobar Administration ... on 16 December, 2025 In The High Court At Calcutta [Circuit Bench At Port Blair] *** Wpa/602/2025 Shri U. Udaiyar Vs. The Andaman and Nicobar Administration and Others Mr. K. M. B. Jayapal ... for the petitioner Mr. K. Vijay Kumar ... for the private respondent December 16, 1. The writ application has been preferred praying for direction upon the respondent authorities more particularly respondent No.2 herein to refrain from issuing bar license in the name of the private respondent for premise in question.
texts.facts: 1. The writ application has been preferred praying for direction upon the respondent authorities more particularly respondent No.2 herein to refrain from issuing bar license in the name of the private respondent for premise in question. 2. The petitioner's case in short herein is that he is in possession of the tenanted premises by virtue of a "sub-let" agreement dated 26.08.2011. It is stated in the agreement that the room rented was only for the purpose of business of the petitioner herein. It is the case of the petitioner that due to an understanding between the said parties to the agreement, the wife of the private respondent no.5 Smt. Jayanti Mondal, being the respondent no.6 herein was permitted by the petitioner herein to carry on the business of bar-cum-restaurant in his rented premises. 3. It is further stated by the petitioner that a civil suit filed by him is pending against the private respondent herein restraining him from dispossessing the petitioner from the tenanted premises without due process of law.
texts.arguments: It is thus submitted that as the tenanted premises is in the possession of the petitioner herein and the petitioner at this stage does not wish to permit the wife of the respondent No.5, being the respondent No. 6 herein from carrying on the said business in his tenanted premises, he has prayed for an order restraining the authorities concerned from issuing a fresh license in favour of the respondent No.6. 4. Learned counsel appearing for the respondent No. 5 and 6 submits that paragraph 2 of the said sub-let agreement clearly lays down that the tenancy agreement was valid for the period from 01.09.2011 to 30.08.2014. It is thus submitted that the period of tenancy has expired and the petitioner is liable to vacate the said premises as he is now a trespasser.
texts.respondent_arguments: It is thus submitted that as the tenanted premises is in the possession of the petitioner herein and the petitioner at this stage does not wish to permit the wife of the respondent No.5, being the respondent No. 6 herein from carrying on the said business in his tenanted premises, he has prayed for an order restraining the authorities concerned from issuing a fresh license in favour of the respondent No.6. 4. Learned counsel appearing for the respondent No. 5 and 6 submits that paragraph 2 of the said sub-let agreement clearly lays down that the tenancy agreement was valid for the period from 01.09.2011 to 30.08.2014. It is thus submitted that the period of tenancy has expired and the petitioner is liable to vacate the said premises as he is now a trespasser.
